title: The gap calculation
objectives: Calculate the gap and the withdrawal rate from expenses, other income and corpus.
Work the ₹6 L / ₹2 L / ₹1 Cr example.
body_md:
The gap calculation: annual expenses − other income = what the portfolio must provide. Divide that by the corpus to get the withdrawal rate. Example (illustrative): expenses ₹6 L a year, pension and rent ₹2 L, so the portfolio must provide ₹4 L. From a ₹1 Cr corpus that is a 4% withdrawal rate.

> **Investor takeaway:** Gap = expenses − other income. Rate = gap ÷ corpus.
example: Expenses ₹6 L, pension and rent ₹2 L, corpus ₹1 Cr → gap ₹4 L → 4% withdrawal rate.
say: Annual expenses − other income = what the portfolio must provide.
Divide the gap by the corpus to get the rate.
never: The rate is expenses divided by income.
Other income doesn't reduce the gap.

check.q: Expenses ₹6 L, pension and rent ₹2 L, corpus ₹1 Cr. The withdrawal rate is…
Expenses ₹6 L, pension and rent ₹2 L, corpus ₹1 Cr. The withdrawal rate is:

check.why: The gap calculation: annual expenses − other income = what the portfolio must provide.
